title: The Earth as Transmitter
attribution: A visual interpretation of Gurdjieff's cosmology

primary_source.work: P. D. Ouspensky, In Search of the Miraculous
primary_source.locator: chapter 7; discussions of organic life as Earth's organ of perception and radiation

events.semantics: Planetary influences are received by organic life and mediated to Earth.
events.guard: Particle markers stand for directed influence, not confirmed literal corpuscles.

events.semantics: Organic life participates in receiving and emitting distinct radiations.
events.guard: Do not imply input and output are materially identical or mechanically converted 1:1.

events.semantics: The Moon depends on radiations from organic life for nourishment and maintenance.
events.guard: Moon luminosity is an illustrative response, not rapid physical growth.

events.semantics: Different radiations are directed toward the Sun, planets, and Moon.
events.guard: Destinations are simultaneous cosmic functions, not a simple ladder of eating.

art_direction.layout: Earth central; Sun and planet upper left; Moon right; all paths annotated by captions
art_direction.visual_style: restrained celestial atlas; low-contrast orbital guides; warm and cool accents
art_direction.caption_style: short narrative statements instead of technical notation
art_direction.exception: Globe textures, celestial scales, and choreography are artistic choices, not ontology claims.
